READING

**Establishing a common baseline**

All 640 colonies currently sit on own sites producing honey. Last season they returned GBP 143,000 with no haulage cost. Per-colony blended return: GBP 223.44. The borage component alone is stated at GBP 71 per colony, implying the balance (roughly heather) is about GBP 152 per colony. The migratory side has been idle since 2025, so neither course disturbs the status quo unless we act.

**Course TREVANNOCK – season-by-season arithmetic**

The 400 Vantwyn colonies miss the Kirkhallow borage but, since the problem identifies only the borage as the lost income, I treat heather as recoverable after they return. The incremental P&L per season is:

| Item | GBP |
|---|---|
| Vantwyn fee (400 × 168) | +67,200 |
| Borage foregone (400 × 71) | −28,400 |
| Spray colony losses (9 % × 400 = 36 colonies × 210) | −7,560 |
| Haulage and labour | −6,900 |
| **Net per season** | **+24,340** |

Three seasons: **GBP 73,020**

At the end of 2029 the lorry's vale permit expires and Ravensgate prices the kit at roughly GBP 20,000. The terminal kit value under TREVANNOCK is therefore **GBP 20,000**.

**Course ORMSCLEUCH – capital arithmetic**

Ravensgate pay GBP 96,000 now (offer open until 28 November 2026, after the 31 October Vantwyn deadline, so the sequencing is clean). All 640 colonies stay on own sites; honey income continues at last season's rate. No haulage, no spray losses.

**Direct comparison (undiscounted)**

TREVANNOCK produces GBP 73,020 of operating surplus over three seasons and leaves kit worth GBP 20,000 — a combined GBP 93,020.

ORMSCLEUCH releases GBP 96,000 immediately.

Difference: ORMSCLEUCH ahead by **GBP 2,980** on a flat, undiscounted count. That is close, but it moves in one direction only once time value is introduced.

**Discounting**

At a modest 5 % annual rate:

| Flow | Year | PV |
|---|---|---|
| Vantwyn net (×3 seasons) | 1, 2, 3 | 23,181 + 22,077 + 21,026 = 66,284 |
| Kit salvage 20,000 | 3 | 17,278 |
| **TREVANNOCK total PV** | | **83,562** |

ORMSCLEUCH delivers **GBP 96,000 at Year 0**.

NPV gap: ORMSCLEUCH better by approximately **GBP 12,400**. The gap widens with any rate above 5 %; it never closes because the operating advantage of GBP 24,340 per year is structurally just below the break-even needed to justify deferring the GBP 96,000 receipt.

**The spray-loss figure deserves scrutiny**

The 9 % figure is drawn from a single comparator (Whinnerdale Bees, 2025). Spray regimes vary between seasons and between sites. In a bad season, 12–15 % losses are plausible. At 15 %, replacement costs rise to GBP 12,600 per season; the net per season falls to GBP 19,300 and the three-year total to GBP 57,900 — well below GBP 76,000 of capital advantage. There is no corresponding downside risk for ORMSCLEUCH.

**The Coldharbour and Nyefield option**

This is the most credible argument for TREVANNOCK. Two vale growers are already asking for a rate for 2028, suggesting a market exists beyond Vantwyn. But the option is tightly constrained:

1. While 400 colonies are at Vantwyn (2027–2029), only 240 colonies are available for any additional vale contract.
2. The lorry loses its vale low-emission permit on 1 January 2030 — precisely when the Vantwyn contract closes. Any ambition to build a second generation of vale contracts requires a replacement low-emission vehicle, a capital outlay not costed here.
3. The pattern already established is that pollination relationships in this region do not renew: three contracts placed, three departed. There is no evidence Coldharbour and Nyefield represent a more durable class of customer.

The option is real but small (240 colonies at best in 2028) and sits behind a permit cliff.

**The queen-rearing shed**

Ravensgate's GBP 96,000 covers pallets and lorry only; the shed is in neither course's stated value. Under ORMSCLEUCH the shed remains useful for routine queen-rearing across all 640 colonies. It is not a swing factor but it does mean ORMSCLEUCH does not strip the business of rearing capacity.

**Strategic clarity**

ORMSCLEUCH converts an asset that earned nothing in 2025 and barely covers its own opportunity cost over three years into immediate working capital, and it concentrates the entire enterprise on fourteen sites the business already understands. TREVANNOCK asks the business to operate two distinct models for a return that, discounted and risk-adjusted, is negative relative to selling now.

---

READING
The incremental operating surplus from three Vantwyn seasons (GBP 73,020 undiscounted, GBP 66,284 at 5 % PV) does not recover the capital advantage of selling the kit now at GBP 96,000 rather than at its GBP 20,000 salvage value in 2030; the NPV gap is approximately GBP 12,400 in favour of ORMSCLEUCH before any allowance for spray-loss variance or the lorry-permit cliff that closes the vale option in any case by January 2030.

CALL
ORMSCLEUCH

GROUNDS
The three-season operating surplus from Vantwyn falls short of the capital released by selling the kit now even on undiscounted arithmetic, the gap widens under any positive discount rate, and spray-loss risk plus a record of zero contract renewals only extend it further.
